Subject: AcmeHealth - Private VPC data flow & egress controls (post-call recap)

Hi Emily / Tom

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to make sure we're aligned on AcmeHealth's privacy and network requirements for a Private / VPC deployment of Redwood: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- PII handling: only metadata-less payloads should be stored in hosted components; sensitive PHI/PII must stay within your VPC.
- Data residency: all inference input and model responses must remain in your VPC region (us-east-1) - no cross-region egress without explicit approval.
- Retention & logging: audit logs required for calls to inference endpoints; retention configurable to 90/180/365 days per environment.
- Egress controls: strict outbound rules, allowlist for redwood control plane IPs (if using private control plane) or the option for fully air-gapped on-prem.
- On-prem / air-gapped constraints: if you require air-gap, we'll provide an on-prem bundle but it will require scheduled updates and an offline upgrade process.

Attachments I'm including: a first-pass network diagram (customer-drawn, annotated in the attachment) and our short data retention summary.

Proposed next steps:
1) Dev/IT: please confirm the list of egress IPs/ports you can allow and whether you prefer private control plane (VPC peering) or on-prem bundle. (Action: Tom / IT)
2) Red team: Rishi + Dev to prepare a one-page runbook for audit-log collection and retention controls for Acme's security review. (Action: Rishi, Dev)
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive to map exact network boundaries and NAT/egress proxy behavior. (Action: Marissa -> propose times)

Would love to get the IT constraints by EOD Friday so Rishi/Dev can prep the security packet over the weekend.

Thanks

Thanks Marissa - helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with IT: 

1) Egress model: IT's preference is private control plane with VPC peering and strict allowlist of Redwood control-plane IPs. Full air-gapped on-prem is a blocker for our ML ops team right now due to update cadence, but we'd consider it for a limited pilot if updates can be handled via an approved offline process.
2) Logging/retention: we require audit logs for all inference calls (request metadata only - hashed identifiers ok) and retention to be configurable with an initial default of 90 days.
3) Data residency: confirmed - all inference payloads must remain in our us-east-1 VPC. No copy to other regions.

Tom / IT team, can you confirm whether outbound HTTP(S) to the listed Redwood IPs (we'll share internal allowlist) is acceptable, or if we need to route via a proxy?

We can do the deep-dive next Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon. Marissa, please send a couple of slots.

Emily Zhang
Head of Data Privacy, Acme Health
emily.zhang@acmehealth.com

Looping in some technical notes we should share with Acme ahead of the deep-dive: 

- Control plane options:
  * Private control plane (recommended): VPC peering or PrivateLink; requires an allowlist of our control-plane IP range and a mutual TLS certificate for the control channel. No inference payloads leave customer VPC; metadata-only telemetry (heartbeats/metrics) can be routed via the control plane if approved.
  * On-prem bundle: we can ship an appliance/container bundle for air-gapped installs; upgrades are manual via signed artifacts - SLA and support scope differ.

- Egress & proxying:
  * If IT must proxy egress, we support outbound HTTPS to our endpoints via the proxy; we'll provide a list of FQDNs and cert pinning guidance.
  * For strict allowlist environments, we'll provide IP ranges per region (will send in a follow-up).

- Logging & retention:
  * Audit logs can be configured to store only hashed request IDs and timestamps; payload-level logs are always opt-in and can be disabled entirely.
  * Retention windows (90/180/365) are configurable per-environment; exportable to your SIEM via secure S3/Cloudwatch exports.

- Compliance artifacts we can share in the technical deep-dive: SOC 2 summary, encryption-at-rest/in-transit diagrams, and a sample audit-log schema.

I'll draft the one-page runbook Rishi mentioned and attach the IP ranges in my next email.

Dev
